Source: Simon Ch. 4, Section 4, 4.1-4.9 (monotonicity for L^p mean curvature, with the coefficient kappa := (p - n)/(4p) of 4.2; cf. simongmt Chapter04.lpMeanCurvatureKappa and LpAnnularCorrection), which is fact (M) of the parent-supplied proof. The only properties of the tangent planes used in Simon's derivation are that, mu-a.e. on the ball where the radial test fields live, V.tangentProj x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace, and that x -> V.tangentProj x is measurable there (needed so that the integrals below are the genuine integrals, since a Bochner integral of a non-measurable function is 0 by convention); both are taken as hypotheses, so no general existence or measurability theorem for approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.9) is needed.

Notation. mu := V.weight, r(x) := |x - y|, B_rho := closed ball B_rho(y), Bo_rho := open ball. kappa := (p - n)/(4p) = (1 - n/p)/4 in (0, 1/4). For x with V.tangentProj x = p_P (P of dimension n) write grad^perp r := grad r - p_P(grad r), so |p_P grad r|^2 = 1 - |grad^perp r|^2 for x != y. ||H|| := (integral over B_R of |H|^p dmu)^{1/p}.

For eps in (0, 1/2) fix a C-infinity nonincreasing phi_eps : R -> [0, 1] with phi_eps = 1 on (-infinity, 1 - eps] and phi_eps = 0 on [1, infinity), chosen so that phi_eps increases pointwise to the indicator of (-infinity, 1) as eps decreases to 0. X is C^1 (phi_eps(r/rho) is constant near x = y) with compact support in B_rho, contained in Bo_R, contained in U, so it is admissible in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H.

subproblem.title: Continuous mean curvature is locally L^p (Step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu_V, and H, h : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l) with h continuous on U and H = h mu_V-a.e. Then for every real p > 0, H is locally in L^p(mu_V) in U: the integral over K of |H|^p dmu_V is finite for every compact K contained in U (V.LocallyLp H p).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H h : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), ContinuousOn h U → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, H x = h x) → ∀ p : ℝ, 0 < p → V.LocallyLp H p
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 7.1, second assertion: H = h with h continuous, so H is locally bounded and lies in L^p_loc for every p). Notation: mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta), where M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult and H^n := muHE[n]. Fix p > 0.

1. Let K be a compact subset of U. Because h is continuous on U and K is a compact subset of U, the function |h| is bounded on K: there is A >= 0 with |h(x)| <= A for every x in K.

2. mu(K) < infinity. K is compact, hence closed, hence Borel. By the definition of the weight, mu(K) = integral over K of ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) = integral over M cap K of ofReal(theta(x)) dH^n(x) <= integral over M cap K of |theta| dH^n. The last integral is finite because theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K (the structure field integrableOn_mult of V applied to the compact set K, which lies in U).

3. Since H = h mu-a.e., also H = h almost everywhere for mu restricted to K. Hence the extended-real integrals agree: integral over K of ||H(x)||_e^p dmu = integral over K of ||h(x)||_e^p dmu.

4. For x in K we have ||h(x)||_e <= ofReal(A), and t -> t^p is nondecreasing on [0, infinity] because p > 0, so ||h(x)||_e^p <= ofReal(A)^p. Therefore integral over K of ||h||_e^p dmu <= ofReal(A)^p * mu(K) (integral of a constant over K).

5. ofReal(A)^p is finite (finite base, positive exponent) and mu(K) is finite by step 2, so integral over K of ||H||_e^p dmu < infinity by steps 3 and 4. Since K was an arbitrary compact subset of U, this is exactly V.LocallyLp H p.

mu_V(K) is finite because theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K

subproblem.title: Translation invariance of rectifiable varifolds with generalized mean curvature
subproblem.statement: Let V = v(M, theta) be a rectifiable n-varifold in U, a subset of R^(n+l), and xi in R^(n+l); put tau(x) = x - xi. There is a rectifiable n-varifold V' in tau(U) with carrier tau(M), multiplicity y -> theta(y + xi), weight mu_V' equal to the image measure tau_# mu_V, and support spt V' = tau(spt V), such that whenever V has generalized mean curvature H in U, V' has generalized mean curvature y -> H(y + xi) in tau(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ), ∃ V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => x - ξ) '' U), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier ∧ (∀ y, V'.mult y = V.mult (y + ξ)) ∧ V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ξ) ∧ V'.support = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.support ∧ ∀ H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun y => H (y + ξ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (Inv) of the parent-supplied proof (translation invariance), used in its Step 2 to apply Simon's Theorem 5.2 (whose hypotheses 5.1 are centred at 0) at the point xi. Notation: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, mu := V.weight, H^n := muHE[n], tau(x) := x - xi with inverse tau^{-1}(y) = y + xi, U' := tau(U).

Facts used. (I1) tau is an isometric bijection of R^(n+l) onto itself (a homeomorphism and a Borel measurable equivalence), and Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometric bijections: H^n(tau(S)) = H^n(S) for every S (Mathlib IsometryEquiv.hausdorffMeasure_image; muHE[n] is a constant multiple of muH[n]). Consequently the image of H^n restricted to S under tau is H^n restricted to tau(S) (MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map), and, by the change-of-variables formula for measurable equivalences, which needs no measurability of the integrand (Mathlib lintegral_map_equiv, MeasurableEquiv.integral_map), integral over tau(S) of g dH^n = integral over S of g(tau x) dH^n(x) for every g >= 0, and likewise for Bochner integrals. (I2) For a homeomorphism tau and a Borel measure nu, spt(tau_# nu) = tau(spt nu): y is outside spt(tau_# nu) iff some open N containing y has nu(tau^{-1} N) = 0 iff tau^{-1}(y) is outside spt nu.

1. Definition. Put M' := tau(M) and theta'(y) := theta(y + xi); let V' be the varifold in U' with carrier M' and multiplicity theta'. We check the structure fields.

2. Fields. (a) M' is contained in U' because M is contained in U. (b) Null-measurability: M is H^n-null-measurable, so there is a Borel set M0 with H^n(M symmetric-difference M0) = 0; then tau(M0) is Borel and H^n(tau(M) symmetric-difference tau(M0)) = H^n(tau(M symmetric-difference M0)) = 0 by (I1). (c) Countable rectifiability: if M is contained in N0 union the union over j of F_j(R^n), with H^n(N0) = 0 and each F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz, then tau(M) is contained in tau(N0) union the union over j of (tau o F_j)(R^n), H^n(tau(N0)) = 0 by (I1), and tau o F_j is Lipschitz with the same constant. (d) Positivity: if y is in M' then y + xi is in M, so theta'(y) = theta(y + xi) > 0. (e) Measurability: by (I1) the measure H^n restricted to M' is the image of H^n restricted to M under the measurable equivalence tau, and theta' = theta o tau^{-1}; since theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, theta' is a.e.-measurable for the image measure (compose an a.e.-equal measurable representative with tau^{-1}). (f) Local integrability: if K is a compact subset of U', then tau^{-1}(K) = K + xi is a compact subset of U and, by (I1), integral over M' cap K of |theta'| dH^n = integral over M cap (K + xi) of |theta| dH^n < infinity.

3. Weight. For every Borel S, V'.weight(S) = integral over S cap M' of ofReal(theta') dH^n = integral over tau^{-1}(S) cap M of ofReal(theta) dH^n (by the change of variables in (I1) for the measurable equivalence tau, applied to the function indicator(S) * ofReal(theta'), which need not be measurable) = mu(tau^{-1}(S)) = (mu.map tau)(S). Two Borel measures agreeing on Borel sets are equal, so V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - xi). Consequently, for every Borel g >= 0 and every mu-integrable g, integral of g d(V'.weight) = integral of g(tau x) dmu(x).

4. Support. V'.support = U' cap spt(V'.weight) = tau(U) cap tau(spt mu) by step 3 and (I2) = tau(U cap spt mu) since tau is injective = tau(V.support).

5. Tangent projections. For every y, every r and every subspace P: blowUpMap y r '' M' = { r^{-1}((x - xi) - y) : x in M } = blowUpMap (y + xi) r '' M; theta'(y + r z) = theta((y + xi) + r z); and theta'(y) = theta(y + xi). Hence, after rewriting the image sets by set extensionality and the multiplicity arguments by add_right_comm (then funext/propext), the proposition HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' theta' y P equals the proposition HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta (y + xi) P (the dimension condition is identical). Therefore the two existence propositions in the definition of tangentProj coincide, the two dependent if-then-else expressions are equal, and V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + xi) for every y. For a C^1 field X' put X := X' o tau; by the chain rule (D tau = identity) DX(x) = DX'(tau x), hence V'.divM X'(tau x) = trace(DX'(tau x) o V'.tangentProj(tau x)) = trace(DX(x) o V.tangentProj(x)) = V.divM X(x) for every x.

6. Generalized mean curvature. Assume V has generalized mean curvature H in U and set H' := H(. + xi) = H o tau^{-1}.
(a) Local integrability of H' on U' for V'.weight: let y in U' and x := y + xi in U. There is a set N in the filter nhdsWithin(x, U) on which H is integrable for mu; then tau(N) belongs to nhdsWithin(y, U') because tau is a homeomorphism with tau(U) = U', and by step 3 integral over tau(N) of |H'| d(V'.weight) = integral over N of |H| dmu < infinity.
(b) First variation: let X' : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l) be C^1 with compact support and tsupport X' contained in U'. Then X := X' o tau is C^1, has compact support, and tsupport X = tau^{-1}(tsupport X') is contained in U. By step 3 and step 5, integral of V'.divM X' d(V'.weight) = integral of V'.divM X'(tau x) dmu(x) = integral of V.divM X dmu = - integral of <X, H> dmu (generalized mean curvature of V) = - integral of <X'(tau x), H'(tau x)> dmu(x) = - integral of <X', H'> d(V'.weight). Together with (a) this says V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun y => H (y + xi)).

All five asserted properties (carrier, multiplicity, weight, support, transfer of generalized mean curvature) are established in steps 1, 3, 4 and 6.

verify the structure fields using isometry invariance of H^n
the weight of V' is tau_# mu_V and its support is tau(spt V)
blow-ups coincide, so tangentProj' y = tangentProj(y + xi) and divM transforms covariantly
transfer local integrability and the first variation identity by change of variables

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent-supplied proof, i.e. the first paragraph of Simon's printed proof of Theorem 7.1 (Ch. 5, p. 127): 'Since the scaled L^p norm of H tends to 0 and omega_n^{-1} rho^{-n} mu_V(B_rho(xi)) tends to 1, we can choose rho > 0 such that the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 hold, so, after applying the appropriate translation and orthogonal transformation, the required u exists with graph u = spt V cap B_{gamma rho}(0)'. Uses the hypothesis AllardRegularityTheorem (Simon 5.2) and the sibling dohr_translate_varifold. Notation: mu := V.weight, theta := V.mult, omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, balls closed unless called open, beta := 1 - n/p.

1. Constants. Apply AllardRegularityTheorem to n, l (1 <= n) and p (n < p): there are delta0 in (0,1), gamma in (0,1) and C such that, for every open U0, every varifold V0 in U0, every H0, and all delta, rho with 0 < delta <= delta0 and V0.AllardHypotheses H0 p delta rho, AllardConclusion V0 p delta rho gamma C holds. Put delta := delta0. Note 0 < beta < 1.

2. Translation. Let tau(x) := x - xi. By dohr_translate_varifold there is a varifold V' in U' := tau(U) with V'.mult y = theta(y + xi), mu' := V'.weight = mu.map tau, V'.support = tau(V.support), and, because V has generalized mean curvature H in U, V' has generalized mean curvature H' := H(. + xi) in U'. U' is open since tau is a homeomorphism. Because tau is a measurable equivalence, mu'(S) = mu(tau^{-1}(S)) for Borel S and integral of g dmu' = integral of g(tau x) dmu(x) for Borel g >= 0; in particular mu'(B_r(0)) = mu(B_r(xi)) and integral over B_r(0) of ||H'||_e^p dmu' = integral over B_r(xi) of ||H||_e^p dmu.

3. Choice of the scale rho. Since U is open and xi in U, fix r0 > 0 with B_{r0}(xi) contained in U, and put L := integral over B_{r0}(xi) of ||H||_e^p dmu, which is finite by V.LocallyLp H p (B_{r0}(xi) is a compact subset of U). V.HasDensity xi 1 says mu(B_r(xi)) / (omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r decreases to 0. Hence we may choose rho in (0, r0] such that for every r in (0, rho]: (a) 0 < mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n; and moreover (b) rho^beta L^{1/p} <= delta (possible because beta > 0, so rho^beta -> 0).

4. xi lies in spt V. xi is in U. If N is an open set containing xi, then B_r(xi) is contained in N for some r in (0, rho], so mu(N) >= mu(B_r(xi)) > 0 by 3(a); hence xi is in spt mu and so in V.support. Therefore 0 = tau(xi) belongs to tau(V.support) = V'.support.

5. Allard hypotheses for V' at (p, delta, rho). (i) rho > 0. (ii) V' has generalized mean curvature H' in U' (step 2). (iii) theta' >= 1 mu'-a.e.: since mu' is the image of mu under the measurable equivalence tau, 'for mu'-a.e. y, 1 <= V'.mult y' is equivalent to 'for mu-a.e. x, 1 <= V'.mult(tau x) = theta(x)', which is a hypothesis. (iv) 0 is in V'.support (step 4). (v) B_rho(0) = tau(B_rho(xi)) is contained in tau(U) = U'. (vi) mu'(B_rho(0)) = mu(B_rho(xi)) <= ofReal((1 + delta) omega_n rho^n) by 3(a). (vii) integral over B_rho(0) of ||H'||_e^p dmu' = integral over B_rho(xi) of ||H||_e^p dmu <= L (B_rho(xi) is contained in B_{r0}(xi)), so (rho^{p-n} * that integral)^{1/p} <= (rho^{p-n})^{1/p} L^{1/p} = rho^beta L^{1/p} <= delta by 3(b); i.e. V'.scaledLpNorm H' p 0 rho <= ofReal(delta). Thus V'.AllardHypotheses H' p delta rho holds with 0 < delta <= delta0, and step 1 gives AllardConclusion V' p delta rho gamma C.

6. Unpacking the conclusion. Put R := gamma rho > 0 and Bbar := closed ball B^n_R(0) in R^n. There are a linear isometry q of R^(n+l) and u : R^n -> R^l with u C^1 on Bbar (ContDiffOn on the closed ball), u(0) = 0, D_Bbar u(0) = 0 (derivative within Bbar), V'.support cap B_R(0) = q(graph of u over Bbar) cap B_R(0) (closed balls), and rho^{-1} sup_Bbar |u| + sup_Bbar |D_Bbar u|_HS + rho^beta sup_{x != y in Bbar} |D_Bbar u(x) - D_Bbar u(y)|_HS / |x - y|^beta <= C delta^{1/(2n+2)} < infinity (sums of suprema in [0, infinity]). Set Q := q^{-1}, again a linear isometry. Since R < rho <= r0, closed B_R(xi) is contained in closed B_rho(xi), which is contained in U.

7. Regularity on the open ball B := open B^n_R(0). B is open and contained in Bbar, so u is C^1 on B. For x in B the closed ball Bbar is a neighbourhood of x, hence the derivative within Bbar equals the derivative: D_Bbar u(x) = Du(x) (fderivWithin of a neighbourhood equals fderiv). In particular fderiv u 0 = 0, because 0 is in B.

8. Hoelder bound. The third summand in step 6 is finite and rho^beta > 0, so K := sup_{x != y in Bbar} |D_Bbar u(x) - D_Bbar u(y)|_HS / |x - y|^beta is a finite real number >= 0. For x != y in B, using step 7 and the inequality ||A||_op <= |A|_HS (for v = sum v_i e_i, |Av| <= sum |v_i| |A e_i| <= |v| (sum |A e_i|^2)^{1/2} by Cauchy-Schwarz) we get ||Du(x) - Du(y)|| <= K |x - y|^beta. For x = y both sides are 0 because beta > 0. Hence there is K with ||fderiv u x - fderiv u y|| <= K ||x - y||^(1 - n/p) for all x, y in B.

9. Graph identity on the open ball. Q is a bijective linear isometry with Q(closed B_R(0)) = closed B_R(0); applying Q to the identity of step 6 gives Q(V'.support) cap closed B_R(0) = graph of u over Bbar cap closed B_R(0). Intersecting both sides with the open ball B_R(0) (contained in the closed ball) gives Q(V'.support) cap B_R(0) = graph of u over Bbar cap B_R(0). Since |(x, u(x))|^2 = |x|^2 + |u(x)|^2 >= |x|^2, a graph point (x, u(x)) in the open ball B_R(0) has |x| < R, i.e. x in B; hence graph of u over Bbar cap B_R(0) = graph of u over B cap B_R(0). Finally V'.support = tau(V.support), so Q '' ((fun x => x - xi) '' V.support) cap ball 0 R = graphOver u (ball 0 R) cap ball 0 R.

Steps 6-9 give R > 0, Q, u with closed B_R(xi) contained in U, u C^1 on ball 0 R, u(0) = 0, fderiv u 0 = 0, the (1 - n/p)-Hoelder bound for fderiv u on ball 0 R, and the graph identity, as claimed.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the second half of Step 2 and Step 3 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 7.1, p. 128: 'Since theta is integer valued and < 2 a.e., we have theta = 1 H^n-a.e. on graph u; but graph u is a C^1 submanifold so then Theta^n(mu_V, x) = 1 at every point of graph u'), with the multiplicity-one step done by the monotonicity formula with the corrected constant kappa = (p-n)/(4p) and the omega_n-normalized additive error. The only change from the parent text is that the bound A_h R^{1-n/p} mu(B_{2t0}(xi))^{1/p} for the scaled L^p norm of H is replaced by the equivalent bound R^{1-n/p} (integral over B_{2t0}(xi) of |H|^p dmu)^{1/p}, which needs only H in L^p_loc. The identity Theta = theta mu-a.e. (fact F1 of the parent) and the lower bound Theta >= 1 on spt V (Simon 4.10(1)) are derived here inside the graph region from (Leb), the sibling dohr_c1_graph_density_one and the sibling dohr_local_monotonicity; the tangent-plane hypothesis of the latter is supplied by the sibling dohr_graph_tangent_planes, so no general existence theorem for approximate tangent spaces is used.

Notation. mu := V.weight, M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu, H^n := muHE[n], omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, kappa := (p - n)/(4p) > 0. Balls are closed unless called open; B_r(y) denotes the closed ball, Bo_r(y) the open ball. T(y) := Q(y - xi) is an isometric bijection of R^(n+l) with inverse A(z) := xi + Q^{-1} z, and T maps Bo_r(xi), B_r(xi) onto Bo_r(0), B_r(0). G(x) := (x, u(x)), Gamma := G(Bo^n_R(0)). The graph hypothesis T(Sigma) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0) is equivalent to Sigma cap Bo_R(xi) = A(Gamma cap Bo_R(0)). By hypothesis theta is a positive integer mu-a.e.; in particular theta >= 1 mu-a.e.

Facts and siblings used. (F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support); mu = theta H^n restricted to M with theta > 0 on M, so for measurable S: mu(S) = integral over S cap M of theta dH^n, and mu(S cap M) = 0 iff H^n(S cap M) = 0. (TP) Sibling dohr_graph_tangent_planes (applied with s := R, using B_R(xi) contained in U): x -> V.tangentProj x is a.e.-strongly measurable for V.weight restricted to Bo_R(xi), and for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi), V.tangentProj y is the orthogonal projection onto Q^{-1}(range DG(x)) where T(y) = G(x); this subspace has dimension n because DG(x) v = (v, Du(x) v) is injective. Since mu(Bo_R(xi) minus Sigma) = 0 and every y in Sigma cap Bo_R(xi) has T(y) = G(x) for some x in Bo^n_R(0), we get: for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi) there is an n-dimensional subspace P with V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection. Both properties pass to every open ball Bo_{R'}(y') contained in Bo_R(xi) (for measurability: AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with Measure.restrict_mono). (M) Sibling dohr_local_monotonicity: if y' in U, R' > 0, B_{R'}(y') contained in U, the tangent-plane condition holds mu-a.e. on Bo_{R'}(y') and x -> V.tangentProj x is a.e.-strongly measurable for V.weight restricted to Bo_{R'}(y') (by (TP) both hold whenever Bo_{R'}(y') is contained in Bo_R(xi)), 0 < Lambda <= 1 and (R'^{p-n} integral over B_{R'}(y') of |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= kappa Lambda, then there is F with |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda and e^{-Lambda} <= F(r) <= e^{Lambda} on (0, R') such that Phi(r) := F(r) r^{-n} mu(B_r(y')) + F(r) - 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R'), and the density Theta(y') := lim_{r -> 0+} mu(B_r(y'))/(omega_n r^n) exists (V.HasDensity y' Theta(y')) with omega_n Theta(y') = lim_{r -> 0+} Phi(r). (Leb) Besicovitch differentiation [Simon Ch. 1, 3.11-3.17; Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv]: if lambda and nu are finite Borel measures on R^(n+l) with lambda = f nu (f >= 0 nu-integrable), then for nu-a.e. y, lambda(B_r(y))/nu(B_r(y)) -> f(y) as r -> 0+. (C4) Sibling dohr_c1_graph_density_one: for every x in Bo^n_R(0), H^n(Gamma cap B_r(G(x)))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r -> 0+. (Iso) H^n(T(S)) = H^n(S) for every S (isometry invariance).

1. A finite graph piece. Put R1 := R/2 and B1 := Bo_{R1}(xi), contained in U since B_R(xi) is. Gamma1 := Sigma cap B1 = A(G(D1)) with D1 := {x in Bo^n_R(0) : |G(x)| < R1}, contained in Bo^n_{R1}(0) because |G(x)| >= |x|. On the compact convex ball B^n_{R1}(0) (inside Bo^n_R(0)) Du is continuous, hence bounded, so G is Lipschitz there and H^n(Gamma1) = H^n(G(D1)) < infinity (Lipschitz image bound for Hausdorff measure and (Iso)). Gamma1 is relatively closed in B1, hence Borel. Let nu := H^n restricted to Gamma1, a finite Borel measure.

2. Density of nu at its points. Let y in Gamma1. Then T(y) is in T(Sigma) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0), so T(y) = G(x) with x in Bo^n_R(0). For 0 < r < R1 - |y - xi| we have B_r(y) contained in B1 and B_r(T(y)) contained in Bo_{R1}(0), which is contained in Bo_R(0); hence nu(B_r(y)) = H^n(Sigma cap B_r(y)) = H^n(A(Gamma cap Bo_R(0)) cap B_r(y)) = H^n(Gamma cap B_r(G(x))) by (Iso). By (C4), nu(B_r(y))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1. In particular nu(B_r(y)) > 0 and nu(B_r(y)) <= 2 omega_n r^n for all small r > 0.

3. mu on B1 has density theta 1_M with respect to nu. B1 is contained in U, so B1 minus Sigma = B1 minus spt mu and mu(B1 minus Sigma) = 0 by (F2). For Borel S contained in B1: mu(S) = mu(S cap Sigma) = integral over S cap Sigma cap M of theta dH^n = integral over S of f dnu with f := theta 1_M (>= 0 on Gamma1). mu(B1) <= mu(B_R(xi)) < infinity (the closed ball B_R(xi) is a compact subset of U, so theta is H^n-integrable on M cap B_R(xi)). So lambda := mu restricted to B1 is a finite Borel measure and lambda = f nu, with f nu-integrable.

4. Theta = theta mu-a.e. on B1. By (Leb), for nu-a.e. y in Gamma1: lambda(B_r(y))/nu(B_r(y)) -> f(y). For y in B1 and small r, lambda(B_r(y)) = mu(B_r(y)). Multiplying by nu(B_r(y))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1 (step 2): for nu-a.e. y in Gamma1, mu(B_r(y))/(omega_n r^n) -> f(y), i.e. Theta(y) = f(y) = theta(y) 1_M(y). The exceptional nu-null set is mu-null (lambda << nu by step 3), mu(B1 minus Gamma1) = 0 and mu(complement of M) = 0. Hence: for mu-a.e. y in B1, y is in Gamma1 cap M and Theta(y) = theta(y) (in contract terms, V.HasDensity y (theta y)); in particular Theta(y) >= 1 for mu-a.e. y in B1.

5. Theta >= 1 on Gamma1 (Simon 4.10(1), proved locally with (M)). Let A1 := integral over B_R(xi) of |H|^p dmu < infinity (V.LocallyLp H p; B_R(xi) is a compact subset of U). For t > 0 put Lambda(t) := max{t^{1 - n/p} A1^{1/p}/kappa, t}; Lambda(t) > 0 and Lambda(t) -> 0 as t -> 0+. Let y in Gamma1 and choose t1 in (0, R/8] with Lambda(t) <= 1 for t <= t1. For 0 < t <= t1 and z with |z - y| <= t: Bo_t(z) and B_t(z) lie in Bo_{R/2 + 2t}(xi), contained in Bo_R(xi), contained in U, and (t^{p-n} integral over B_t(z) of |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= t^{1-n/p} A1^{1/p} <= kappa Lambda(t), so (M) applies at z with R' := t and Lambda := Lambda(t). For 0 < r < t and d := |z - y| this gives omega_n Theta(z) <= Phi_z(r) <= e^{Lambda(t)} r^{-n} mu(B_{r+d}(y)) + Lambda(t); letting r -> t-, omega_n Theta(z) <= e^{Lambda(t)} (1 + d/t)^n omega_n S(2t) + Lambda(t), where S(sigma0) := sup over 0 < sigma <= sigma0 of mu(B_sigma(y))/(omega_n sigma^n) (here t + d <= 2t). By (M) at y, Theta(y) exists and S(sigma0) -> Theta(y) as sigma0 -> 0+. Suppose Theta(y) < 1. Choose eps in (0, 1) with (1 + eps)^n Theta(y) < 1, and then t in (0, t1] so small that c := e^{Lambda(t)} (1 + eps)^n S(2t) + Lambda(t)/omega_n < 1 (possible because, as t -> 0+, Lambda(t) -> 0 and S(2t) -> Theta(y), so c -> (1 + eps)^n Theta(y) < 1). Then Theta(z) <= c < 1 for every z with |z - y| <= eps t. But Bo_{eps t}(y) is contained in B1 for small t (y is in the open set B1) and mu(Bo_{eps t}(y)) > 0 because y is in spt mu, so by step 4 there is z in Bo_{eps t}(y) with Theta(z) = theta(z) >= 1, a contradiction. 6. Carrier versus support on B1. (a) H^n((M cap B1) minus Sigma) = 0: mu((M cap B1) minus Sigma) <= mu(complement of spt mu) = 0 (F2), and these points lie in M where theta > 0, so their H^n measure is 0 (F2). Hence nu(Gamma1 minus M) = 0, i.e. H^n((Sigma cap B1) minus M) = 0. Together: H^n((M cap B1) symmetric-difference (Sigma cap B1)) = 0.

7. Theta < 2 near xi (monotonicity, corrected constant, omega_n-normalized error). Fix t0 in (0, R1/2]; then B_{2 t0}(xi) is contained in B_R(xi), which is contained in U. Let A0 := integral over B_{2 t0}(xi) of |H|^p dmu < infinity (V.LocallyLp H p) and Lambda := min{omega_n, 1}/100, so 0 < Lambda <= 1/100 and Lambda/omega_n <= 1/100. For y in B_{t0}(xi) and 0 < R' <= t0, B_{R'}(y) is contained in B_{2 t0}(xi), so (R'^{p-n} integral over B_{R'}(y) of |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= R'^{1 - n/p} A0^{1/p}. Choose t in (0, t0] with (a) t^{1 - n/p} A0^{1/p} <= kappa Lambda (possible since 1 - n/p > 0) and (b) mu(B_sigma(xi)) <= (11/10) omega_n sigma^n for all 0 < sigma <= 2t (possible since V.HasDensity xi 1). Then Bo_t(y) and B_t(y) are contained in B_{2 t0}(xi), contained in Bo_R(xi) (2 t0 <= R/2), contained in U, so by (a) and (TP) the hypotheses of (M) hold at y with R' := t and this Lambda. 10. Weight on ball xi s. By step 8 the set N := {x in M cap Bo_s(xi) : theta(x) != 1} is mu-null; choose a measurable mu-null set N' containing N. Then H^n(N' cap M) = 0 (by (F2), as theta > 0 on M), so theta = 1 H^n-a.e. on M cap Bo_s(xi). For Borel S: mu(S cap Bo_s(xi)) = integral over S cap Bo_s(xi) cap M of theta dH^n = H^n(S cap Bo_s(xi) cap M) = H^n(S cap Bo_s(xi) cap Sigma), the last equality by step 9 (the two sets differ by an H^n-null set).
